facts.intro: Introduce a recognizable worm gear: a long threaded steel worm lying along the bottom with a red hand crank on its left end, and a large brass toothed wheel above it. Everything is still.
facts.cutaway: Inside are the thread of the worm pressing into the teeth at the bottom of the wheel.
facts.drive: A push turns the crank and the worm. Its thread slides along and pushes the wheel teeth sideways, so the wheel creeps round.
facts.response: The worm keeps turning and the wheel keeps creeping. Each full turn of the worm moves the wheel by exactly one tooth.
facts.hold: No part moves for this explanation. The wheel has twelve teeth, so it needs twelve turns of the worm to go all the way round.
facts.repeat: A second push turns the worm several more times, and the wheel again moves slowly, one tooth for each turn.
facts.limit: The crank turns backwards for a moment. The wheel creeps back by the same number of teeth, so the pair stays in step.
facts.payoff: Crank, worm and wheel work together: many fast turns become one slow turn with a strong push. No motor or casing is shown.
